bib.title: Abstractive Text Summarization using Sequence-to-sequence RNNs and Beyond
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 20th SIGNLL Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning (CoNLL), pages 280-290

question: Can an off-the-shelf attentional encoder-decoder RNN, plus extensions for keywords, rare words and hierarchy, do abstractive summarization well?
hypothesis: Each proposed extension addresses a specific weakness of the basic MT-style model and should add incremental improvement.
contributions: Apply the off-the-shelf attentional encoder-decoder RNN from machine translation to summarization and outperform state-of-the-art on two English corpora
Propose models for summarization-specific problems (feature-rich encoder, switching generator-pointer, hierarchical attention) with further gains
Propose a new multi-sentence summarization dataset (CNN/Daily Mail) and establish benchmarks

method.summary: Bidirectional GRU encoder, unidirectional GRU decoder with attention and the large vocabulary trick, trained on Gigaword headline data; variants add TF/IDF/POS/NER feature embeddings, a switching generator/pointer for OOV words, and word+sentence hierarchical attention. Evaluated with ROUGE on Gigaword, DUC-2004 (zero-shot) and a new CNN/Daily Mail multi-sentence set.

datasets.name: Annotated Gigaword (Rush et al. 2015 preprocessing)
datasets.size: about 3.8M training examples; random 2000 validation and 2000 test examples from about 400K
datasets.split: random 2000 validation, 2000 test (internal test set); also the exact Rush et al. test sample
datasets.source: scripts from Rush et al. (2015), github.com/facebook/NAMAS
datasets.preprocessing: scripts modified to also extract system-generated POS and NER tags; first sentence (or first two) of document as source

datasets.name: DUC 2003/2004
datasets.split: DUC-2004 test; model trained on Gigaword only, not tuned on DUC
datasets.preprocessing: decoder forced to emit exactly 30 words (end-of-summary suppressed)

datasets.name: CNN/Daily Mail (new multi-sentence summarization corpus)
datasets.split: as defined by Hermann et al. scripts
datasets.source: modified Hermann et al. (2015) scripts; anonymized version used
datasets.preprocessing: highlights restored in original order, each treated as a sentence; source vocab 150K, target vocab 60K, source/target at most 800/100 words; training sources average 766 words, 29.74 sentences; summaries 53 words, 3.72 sentences

models.name: words-lvt2k-1sent (baseline attentional enc-dec + LVT)
models.architecture: bidirectional GRU encoder, unidirectional GRU decoder, attention, softmax over target vocab, large vocabulary trick
models.init_from: 200-d word2vec trained on same corpus (Gigaword); updated during training; code started from Kyunghyun Cho's dl4mt-material
models.vocab: Gigaword first-sentence: encoder 119,505, decoder 68,885; LVT restricts decoder to 2,000

other.feats_embedding: input embedding grew from 100 to 155 with features

models.name: words-lvt2k-2sent, -2sent-hieratt, feats-lvt2k-2sent, feats-lvt2k-2sent-ptr
models.architecture: variants: two source sentences; hierarchical word+sentence attention with sentence positional embeddings; feature-rich encoder (POS, NER, discretized TF, IDF); switching generator/pointer

models.name: ABS+ (Rush et al. 2015)
models.architecture: convolutional/attentional encoder with feed-forward decoder plus log-linear extractive model

training.objective: conditional log-likelihood; for pointer model log P(y|x) = sum_i g_i log{P(y_i|y_-i,x)P(s_i)} + (1-g_i) log{P(p(i)|y_-i,x)(1-P(s_i))}
training.epochs: Gigaword: typically converged within 15 epochs; CNN/DM: nearly 35 epochs
training.seq_len: CNN/DM: source at most 800, target at most 100 words
training.regularisation: no dropout or regularization; gradient clipping applied (clip value not stated); early stopping on validation set
training.compute: Gigaword: about 10 hours/epoch (12 for hierarchical attention); CNN/DM: under 5 hours/epoch flat, about 12.5 hours/epoch hierarchical
training.wall_clock: Gigaword 6-8 days to convergence; CNN/DM about 7 days flat, nearly 18 days hierarchical

other.shuffling: training data shuffled every epoch, every 10 batches sorted by length
other.lvt_effect: decoder vocab 2,000 cuts training time per epoch by nearly three times and converges in 50%-75% of epochs
other.pointer_supervision: explicit pointer given when summary word is OOV for decoder vocab; ties broken to first occurrence

inference.max_tokens: 30 words (Gigaword); exactly 30 words forced for DUC

parameters.pointer_decision: arg max of switch posterior at each step

other.throughput: about 20 summaries/s on one GPU, batch 1 (Gigaword); 2/s flat and 1.5/s hierarchical on CNN/DM

limits: Best models (2sent, feats, ptr, hieratt) could not be evaluated on the Rush et al. test sample because it has one source sentence and no NLP annotations, so the comparison with ABS+ uses only the baseline model.
Pointer model gives accurate pointing but its overall improvement is not significant; authors expect more impact with heavier-tailed rare word distributions.
On CNN/Daily Mail, pointer and hierarchical models fail to beat the baseline; results called preliminary.
Generated CNN/DM summaries often repeat the same sentence or phrase.
Significance reported only for the best performing models; single runs, no seeds.
Concurrent Chopra et al. (2016) reports slightly better Gigaword numbers on all three ROUGE F1 metrics.
Weakness conceded: capturing the meaning of complex sentences; ROUGE misses meaningful paraphrase.
